text:
{
  "final_quality": "tie",
  "reason": "Both final plans support the same consequential outcome: retain the installed adapter on a private candidate, publish the complete batch once, preserve unrelated inventory, recover through fresh attempts and idempotent replay, and require actual CLI and failure tests during implementation. Both have supporting adapter and publication evidence and reject unsafe storage states. A explicitly gates full acceptance on interruption semantics; B identifies rollback after visible publication as unavailable and disclaims the stronger promise. Neither establishes that promise or product acceptance. A's additional mechanics and stricter gate do not demonstrate a better final outcome, while B's larger review-stage evidence gain does not outweigh evidence A had already obtained.",
  "decisive_evidence": [
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Validate full input, copy complete database to private candidate, apply through installed adapter, verify/close candidate, publish once.",
      "locator": "A.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Interfaces and boundaries",
      "consequence": "Runtime adapter failures remain isolated from the visible inventory; the design does not rely on prevalidation or an ineffective outer transaction."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Publish with one same-directory os.replace after a full sqlite3.backup snapshot, adapter row application, closed/checked stage, preserved POSIX mode and fsync.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: publication experiment decision.md, opening paragraph",
      "consequence": "B selects the same consequential isolation and publication strategy, using a SQLite snapshot instead of A's full-file copy."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Retry and repeat publish [(keep,9),(new,4),(old,7)] with unrelated table/index intact, even with an orphan remaining.",
      "locator": "A.planning_artifacts: run/notes/planning-experiments.md, Experiment 2 evaluation and cleanup",
      "consequence": "Earlier observations support preservation, recovery and logical idempotence before Plan Improve; these are not gains attributable to its later transport probe."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "RECOVERY/replay pre-replace complete table, metadata, integrity, permission preserved",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: publication_probe.attempt1.log, pre-replace recovery output",
      "consequence": "Completed subcases supply useful publication and recovery evidence despite the script's later failure in the WAL negative-control observer."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Any unresolved A5 prevents full R-1 acceptance, even if other tests pass.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.work_items, W2 context",
      "consequence": "A expressly preserves the semantic acceptance condition; planning completion is not unconditional readiness."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "This is an explicit planning interpretation/limitation of literal \"any interrupted import\", not proof of that stronger promise.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Interfaces and boundaries",
      "consequence": "B distinguishes its observed commit-point behavior from the unavailable stronger guarantee rather than claiming the probe establishes user intent."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "No product source/tests authored, no acceptance passed.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.summary",
      "consequence": "A's successful prototypes and baseline remain planning evidence, with durable feature acceptance still due."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "A2/A3/A5 feasibility probes are not product acceptance; retain their limits.",
      "locator": "B.plans[0].final.work_items, W2 context",
      "consequence": "B likewise retains implementation obligations after resolving its mechanical feasibility questions."
    }
  ],
  "initial_plan_and_rework": "A's initial plan already contained characterized publication, worker-exit isolation, sidecar rejection, meaningful interruption/recovery checks and the open semantic gate. Its review concretized target eligibility and transport/mode policy, then repaired conflicting feature and semantic ownership. Its earlier test-strategy review had already added mid-candidate interruption and broader prepublication failures; those should not be counted as later Plan Improve gains. B's initial plan correctly left publication feasibility conditional. Review supplied consequential snapshot, interruption, retry and WAL evidence, selected a supported storage policy, specified alias-check ordering and cleanup coverage, and aligned helper locations and acceptance guards. B therefore gained more mechanical readiness during review, while A entered review with that readiness already supported. Both ownership repairs were useful reductions in downstream ambiguity, without redesigning the existing W1-to-W2 dependency.",
  "earlier_evidence_value": "Exact adapter inspection and earlier characterization legitimately supported rejecting live application and caller rollback in both plans. Unchanged baseline evidence remained reusable and established only existing single-row behavior. A's earlier publication observations supported its initial design. B legitimately reused completed DELETE-mode assertions from its failed compound probe and reran the repaired WAL observer only; neither the first script nor the targeted rerun was represented as a successful full product test. Experiment timing, quantity and whole-script exit status alone do not determine evidence value.",
  "harms_or_lost_requirements": [
    "The literal guarantee of old-state restoration after already-visible publication remains unfulfilled in both. A gates acceptance on resolving its interpretation; B explicitly identifies the stronger guarantee as unavailable. Neither supplies user agreement resolving that boundary.",
    "Both restrict supported journal/path states and require safe rejection elsewhere. These limits are disclosed; neither demonstrates unrestricted SQLite import support.",
    "No consequential seed mutation, unauthorized external effect, sensitive-data exposure or running-resource leak is established. Retained evidence files and the deliberate policy of leaving crash candidates inert do not by themselves establish material harm. Extra commands are cost observations unless a consequential regression is shown."
  ],
  "individual_judgment_corrections": [
    "No clear factual contradiction is established in either judgment's core account of adapter isolation, publication evidence or planned acceptance. Their broad statements that planning obligations are fulfilled must retain the documented interruption limits; neither plan proves literal rollback after publication.",
    "B's final A3 marks the physical commit-boundary observation as probed. Reading that disposition as experimental resolution of user intent would be incorrect; its architecture and decision note expressly disclaim the stronger promise.",
    "A's transport-probe criticism is a judgment about marginal investigation value, not a factual finding of harm. JSON stdin and mode preservation were already intended, but review did concretize target eligibility. The small successful probe still does not establish worker failure handling or comprehensive permission behavior.",
    "Both judgments correctly note that helper/owner corrections did not create a new dependency. Those corrections nevertheless removed conflicting implementation guidance and should be credited as useful review rework.",
    "The specific allegation that A's baseline and absent-module invocations were redundant cannot be independently resolved from this paired view: the cited raw command sequence is omitted. It should remain an unresolved cost observation, not a demonstrated quality regression."
  ],
  "confidence": "high",
  "limits": [
    "Both outcomes are plans; the CLI, helpers and durable feature tests remain unimplemented. Planning completion and the passing baseline are not release evidence.",
    "Observations cover the supplied local runtime and process interruption, not power loss, other filesystems or other platforms.",
    "The omitted raw command transcript prevents independent auditing of every invocation, earlier scratch cleanup and event-specific cost claim. The retained publication scripts, logs and notes support bounded conclusions without settling those omitted details.",
    "This diagnostic comparison does not demonstrate a broader treatment effect or justify a release decision."
  ]
}
requested_model_attestation: Exact model and effort requested; provider served identity not independently exposed.
